title: Gemini thoughtSignature is a sibling of functionCall on the Part, never nested inside it
answers: Gemini multi-turn tool calling fails through AI Gateway thought signature rejected
Gemini function call thought signature dropped from response
where does thoughtSignature go in Gemini functionCall part
Gemini 3 thought signature tool call gateway error
body:
Symptom: Multi-turn tool calling through the AI Gateway to Gemini is rejected, or the model's thought signature never reaches the client after a tool call.
Root cause: GeminiAdapter.chat_to_model nested thoughtSignature inside the functionCall dict, and GeminiAdapter._convert_function_call_to_openai_choice only read it from inside functionCall, so it was dropped.
Fix pattern: Keep thoughtSignature on the Part dict next to {"functionCall": ...} on both paths. Write it as part["thoughtSignature"]; read it from the part first, then fall back to function_call for older responses that nested it.
Constraints: The read-side nested fallback is intentional for older responses and must stay. Write-side output must never nest it, since Gemini rejects that shape.
applies: Any change to Gemini request building or response parsing in mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py, and the Vertex AI provider that reuses the Gemini request shape.
says: Gemini multi-turn tool calling fails because the provider rejects the thought signature.
Thought signatures are missing from the gateway response following a model function call.
Pass through the model reasoning signature correctly during multi-turn function calling interactions.
Clients do not receive the thought signature generated by Gemini during tool execution.
search: Gemini requests and responses must place thoughtSignature as a sibling of functionCall on the Part dictionary rather than nesting it inside functionCall. In mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py, GeminiAdapter.chat_to_model writes part["thoughtSignature"], while GeminiAdapter._convert_function_call_to_openai_choice reads from the part first and falls back to function_call for legacy nested responses. The write side must never nest thoughtSignature because Gemini rejects that structure, but the read fallback must remain for older responses. This applies to request formatting and response parsing in mlflow/gateway/providers/gemini.py and the Vertex AI provider.
